detailed_analysis: The fitted centers give a rutile-TiO2 fingerprint: Eg-analog dominant band at 442.1+/-0.4 cm-1, A1g-analog at 609.7+/-0.04 cm-1, a broad multiphonon/second-order band at 233.1+/-0.08 cm-1 (fitted essentially pure-Lorentzian, eta~0, consistent with a second-order overtone feature), plus a sharp low-frequency line (B1g) at 142.3+/-0.08 cm-1. Weak features at ~703 and ~805 cm-1 are consistent with additional second-order/combination bands of rutile. Critically, the classic rutile assignment is that the ~447 mode (Eg) and ~612 (A1g) are the two strong first-order modes and ~235 is a broad second-order band; the strong-peak positions here match rutile within a few cm-1. The absence of an intense 144 cm-1 line (which would dominate for anatase) argues against anatase. The Eg-region decomposition into a 442 core plus 405 and 448 flanking shoulders is a superposition trick to reproduce the band's asymmetry/flat top; these subcomponents have boundary-pinned eta and inflated errors, so their individual areas (relative intensities 0.068 and 0.315) should NOT be interpreted as separate physical modes. The composite Eg area (effective center 440.95, effective FWHM 37.9) is the meaningful quantity. Residuals remain systematically ~3 sigma at the strong bands even after adding shoulders, exactly the signature of forcing symmetric profiles onto asymmetric lattice modes (temperature/anharmonic broadening of rutile's Eg band is well documented). Fit quality R2=0.9993 is high but, per domain rules, does not by itself validate the decomposition given the residual structure. Baseline is confirmed flat/linear (rolling-min area fraction 0.46), so this is not fluorescence-dominated. Band summary (center cm-1, relative intensity, strongest first): 442 (1.00, composite Eg), 233 (0.31), 611 (0.47), 143 (0.14), 805 (0.034), 703 (0.011). No chemistry (EDX/XRF) was provided, so the identification is pattern-only; rutile is the leading candidate, with anatase disfavored by the missing dominant 144 line and the broad 232 second-order band being characteristic of rutile.

scientific_claims.claim: The Raman spectrum matches rutile TiO2, with first-order modes at 442.1+/-0.4 cm-1 (Eg) and 609.7+/-0.04 cm-1 (A1g) and a broad second-order band at 233.1+/-0.08 cm-1, and no dominant 144 cm-1 anatase line.
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: Distinguishes the rutile polymorph from anatase/brookite, which is critical for photocatalytic, pigment, and high-temperature phase-stability applications where polymorph identity governs function.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone confirmed that an unknown TiO2 sample is the rutile polymorph based on the 447/612 first-order pair plus a broad ~235 second-order band and the absence of a dominant 144 anatase line?

model_type: Sum of 8 pseudo-Voigt peaks on a flat linear baseline (Levenberg-Marquardt / TRF least squares). Bands: B1g ~143 (sharp, Lorentzian-leaning), broad ~232, Eg main ~445, A1g ~611 (broadened low-frequency flank absorbs ~577 shoulder), weak ~700, second-order/overtone ~800 (restored to seeded position, FWHM ~40-50), Eg low-frequency shoulder ~405, Eg high-frequency shoulder ~450 cm-1. The dominant Eg band is decomposed into a symmetric main core plus two flanking symmetric pseudo-Voigt shoulders (superposition, no skewed profiles). peak_6 constrained to 780-820 cm-1 (FWHM<=60) to resolve the 800 band; peak_1 narrowed and pushed toward Lorentzian to reach the ~4000 apex; peak_2 eta free for the 263-335 tail. Center windows: Eg main 437-453, Eg shoulders 395-415 / 448-470, A1g 580-620, others +-15. FWHM>0, amp>0, eta in [0,1]. Flat/linear baseline confirmed (rolling-min baseline area fraction = 0.460, not fluorescence-dominated).

verification_iterations.model: Sum of 6 pseudo-Voigt profiles on a flat linear baseline. Components: (1) B1g ~143 cm⁻¹ sharp, (2) broad multi-phonon/second-order band ~232 cm⁻¹, (3) Eg ~445 cm⁻¹ (dominant), (4) A1g ~611 cm⁻¹, (5) weak band ~700 cm⁻¹, (6) weak broad band ~800 cm⁻¹. Each band = pseudo-Voigt (amplitude, center, FWHM, mixing η). No shoulders/asymmetry detected in zoomed windows, so symmetric profiles are used; will switch a band to an asymmetric profile only if residuals show a dispersive S-shape.

issues.problem: The single pseudo-Voigt at 443 cm⁻¹ cannot reproduce the peak shape; the data shows a broader, flatter-topped/slightly asymmetric band than the fitted symmetric profile.
The rising low-frequency shoulder/foot of the 443 band is not modeled; the fit systematically undershoots the steep rise.
Fit overshoots the high-frequency tail of the main band across the whole window (single-sign residual).

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Add a component seeded near ~450 cm⁻¹ (and/or ~405 cm⁻¹) to resolve the asymmetry/shoulder of the dominant band around peak_3.

verification_iterations.model: Sum of pseudo-Voigt profiles on a flat linear baseline, now comprising 7 (optionally 8) components to fully describe the dominant Eg band region. Retained components: (1) B1g ~143 cm⁻¹ sharp, (2) broad multi-phonon/second-order band ~232 cm⁻¹, (3) Eg main ~445 cm⁻¹ (dominant, symmetric core), (4) A1g ~611 cm⁻¹, (5) weak band ~700 cm⁻¹, (6) weak broad band ~800 cm⁻¹. Added components to resolve the flat-topped/asymmetric shape of the dominant band: (7) low-frequency shoulder of the Eg band seeded near ~405 cm⁻¹ to capture the systematically undershot steep rising edge, and (8) high-frequency shoulder/asymmetry component seeded near ~450 cm⁻¹ to capture the flat-topped asymmetry and correct the overshoot on the falling wing (478.8–550.8 cm⁻¹). This preserves the locked symmetric pseudo-Voigt model (no asymmetric/skewed profiles introduced); apparent asymmetry is represented by superposition of two-to-three symmetric pseudo-Voigt profiles around the main band. Each band remains a pseudo-Voigt with (amplitude, center, FWHM, mixing η).

issues.problem: Fit systematically undershoots the B1g apex (data ~4000 vs fit ~3500) and misfits the surrounding rise/valley shape
Single symmetric pseudo-Voigt cannot reproduce an asymmetric/shouldered A1g band; residual oscillates (excess near 577 and 615, deficit near 595)
Pure-Lorentzian broad band (peak_2 eta≈0) misfits the low-frequency tail decay shape

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Retune within the locked 8-peak model: relax peak_1 (B1g ~143) amplitude/FWHM to reach the true apex, and adjust peak_6 (A1g ~611) center/FWHM/eta to capture the low-frequency shoulder near ~577 cm⁻¹; also let peak_2 eta increase to fix the 275–300 cm⁻¹ tail

verification_iterations.model: Sum of symmetric pseudo-Voigt profiles on a flat linear baseline, comprising 8 components describing the full spectrum (119-1270 cm-1). Components: (1) B1g ~143 cm-1 sharp core, now permitted a more Lorentzian character with a slightly larger width to reach its true apex (~4000 counts) and correctly fill the surrounding rise/valley flanks; (2) broad multi-phonon/second-order band ~232 cm-1, retuned from pure-Lorentzian toward a Voigt mixture (eta > 0) so the low-frequency tail decay through 263-335 cm-1 is reproduced; (3) Eg main ~445 cm-1 (dominant, symmetric core); (4) A1g ~611 cm-1, retuned in center/FWHM/eta to better balance its two flanks; (5) weak band ~700 cm-1; (6) weak broad band ~800 cm-1; (7) low-frequency Eg shoulder ~405 cm-1 capturing the steep rising edge; (8) high-frequency Eg asymmetry/shoulder ~450 cm-1 capturing the flat-topped asymmetry and falling-wing overshoot. The A1g asymmetry (shoulder near ~577 cm-1) is addressed by retuning peak_6 within the locked model rather than adding profiles. The model remains strictly symmetric pseudo-Voigt (no skew/asymmetric functions); all apparent asymmetry is represented by superposition of symmetric components. Each band retains (amplitude, center, FWHM, mixing eta).

issues.problem: A clear, prominent data band peaking near ~800 cm⁻¹ (amplitude ~1000 counts above baseline) is essentially unmodeled — the fit's peak_5 (~715, FWHM 150) and peak_6 (retuned to ~608) do not cover it, leaving the entire band as residual
Fit still undershoots the sharp B1g apex (data ~4000 vs fit ~3200) and misfits the valley shape near 155–175
Broad band tail decay shape is misfit — fit undershoots ~270–290 and overshoots ~295–310

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Add a pseudo-Voigt component seeded at ~800 cm⁻¹ (FWHM ~40–50) to capture the unmodeled band; this is a real feature, not noise.

verification_iterations.model: Sum of 8 symmetric pseudo-Voigt profiles on a flat linear baseline over 119-1270 cm-1. Components: (1) B1g ~143 cm-1 sharp core, more Lorentzian character (eta toward 0.8-1.0), FWHM narrowed to reach true apex (~4000 counts); (2) broad multi-phonon/second-order band ~232 cm-1, Voigt mixture (eta free in [0,1]) to reproduce the 263-335 cm-1 tail decay; (3) Eg main ~445 cm-1 (dominant, symmetric core); (4) A1g ~611 cm-1, retuned in center/FWHM/eta with modest broadening on its low-frequency flank to represent the ~577 cm-1 shoulder now that peak_6 no longer covers it; (5) weak band ~700 cm-1; (6) second-order/overtone band RESTORED to ~800 cm-1 (FWHM ~40-50, amplitude ~1000 counts) — this component was previously misappropriated to ~608 cm-1 and is now returned to its seeded 800 cm-1 role, resolving the dominant unmodeled band; (7) low-frequency Eg shoulder ~405 cm-1 (steep rising edge); (8) high-frequency Eg asymmetry/shoulder ~450 cm-1 (flat-topped asymmetry, falling-wing overshoot). Strictly symmetric pseudo-Voigt; all asymmetry via superposition. Each band: (amplitude, center, FWHM, mixing eta).

issues.problem: Symmetric pseudo-Voigt undershoots the sharp B1g apex (data ~4000 vs fit ~3600) and misfits the valley/rise shape near 155–175
Single symmetric profile leaves a low-frequency shoulder near ~577 cm⁻¹ under-resolved; residual oscillates
Low-frequency tail decay of the broad band slightly misfit
